title: CleitonForge: differential testing for quantum compilers, with declared oracle power
description:
A differential fuzzer for quantum compilers, and a measurement of what its oracles can actually detect. A negative result in differential testing has no meaning without a declared oracle power, and this repository measures that power rather than asserting it.

Two blindness results are established.

First, an outcome-counts oracle has provably and empirically zero power against a global Rz sign convention fault over the gate family {H, X, Z, Ry, Rz, CX, CZ}: 0 of 16418 non-equivalent mutants, 95% Wilson interval [0.000%, 0.023%]. Inverting a single Rz is a different fault class and is ordinarily visible, which the earlier literature conflates.

Second, in quantum error correction, an oracle that derives its reference from the circuit under test has zero power against a deterministically inserted Pauli: 0 of 321 for X and 0 of 211 for Z on a rotated surface code, while detecting every other injected fault class at 100%. A four-instruction witness exhibits two circuits with identical detector error models, identical self-referential detection rates, and cross-referential rates of 0 and 1.

Power throughout is measured against non-equivalent mutants only, with the reference oracle validated by a known-answer battery before use. Every number is printed by a script in research/.

The LaTeX sources under paper/ are working drafts, not peer-reviewed publications.
notes: Preprints under paper/ are drafts. The software and the measurements in research/ are the archived artefact.
